item.title: Feedback wanted on changes to Consumer Reporting Act
item.description:
Feedback wanted on changes to Consumer Reporting Act ddgillis Tue, 09/29/2026 - 13:48

The province is inviting residents and interested stakeholders to share their feedback on laws affecting consumer reporting agencies.

The proposed amendments would remove the requirement for a consumer reporting agency, such as a credit bureau, to maintain a fixed place of business in PEI and would make related changes to support regulatory oversight. The changes would also allow consumers to request and receive a consumer report by telephone, mail or electronically.

“While consumer reporting agencies have traditionally maintained offices in PEI, this is not always possible. We need a mechanism that better reflects how consumers access this service today and aligns with regulatory approaches in the other provinces. The proposed changes will ensure PEI residents can access their consumer report by telephone, mail or electronically, which will bring us in alignment with the rules in most other Canadian provinces.”

- Justice and Public Safety Minister Bloyce Thompson

Consultation documents are available at Department of Justice and Public Safety Public Consultations for people to review. 

Comments in English or French for all documents can be submitted by email to justicepolicy@gov.pe.ca until October 15, 2026.

item.title: Preventive Literacy Intervention (PLI)
item.description:
Preventive Literacy Intervention (PLI) wendygallant Tue, 09/29/2026 - 10:56

The Preventive Literacy Intervention (PLI) is a targeted support service offered to elementary students within the French Language School Board who experience challenges in reading and writing. The intervention is designed to strengthen students’ literacy skills through explicit, systematic, and targeted instruction. The PLI interventionist works in close collaboration with the classroom teacher to identify students’ needs, plan appropriate interventions, and monitor ongoing progress. Interventions focus on the development of phonological awareness, decoding, reading fluency, vocabulary, reading comprehension, and writing skills. Through a preventive, data-informed approach, PLI helps support student achievement and strengthens the foundational literacy skills necessary for long-term academic success.

item.title: Seniors’ Secretariat Grants support projects for seniors
item.description:
Seniors’ Secretariat Grants support projects for seniors jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/29/2026 - 10:15

Community organizations across the province have received funding through the Seniors' Secretariat Grant program to deliver projects that support older adults.

The program is funded through the provincial government and provides grants to community-based organizations for projects that improve the lives of Island seniors. This year, over $140,000 was approved for 62 projects across the province. 

"Thank you to all the organizations whose dedication and passion help make a difference in the lives of Island seniors. By supporting programs that bring people together, we are helping older adults stay connected and engaged as they age in their communities."

- Social Development and Seniors Minister Barb Ramsay

Applications for the most recent round of funding opened in February and closed in March 2026. 

“Across PEI, organizations and communities play an essential role in helping older Islanders stay active, connected and engaged,” said chair of the PEI Seniors' Secretariat Peter Holman. “The PEI Seniors’ Secretariat is proud to support projects that promote healthy aging, strengthen social connection, and enhance the quality of life for older adults.” 

“At Parkview Senior Citizens Club of Summerside, we offer year-round programming for our more than 210 members,” said President of Parkview Seniors Citizens Club Jim Steele. “We appreciate funding from the Seniors Secretariat as it helps to offset a portion of the cost of our social events.”

The Seniors’ Secretariat provides policy and program advice to government and other organizations to improve the quality of life for seniors in Prince Edward Island. 

This grant program supports a key pillar of the Seniors Action Plan 2026-2031 by enhancing the well-being of older adults in PEI.

item.title: PEI history podcast returns for season six
item.description:
PEI history podcast returns for season six jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/29/2026 - 10:05

The PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation is launching season six of the hidden island podcast, which explores Prince Edward Island’s past in new and unexpected ways and shows why it is still relevant today.    

New episodes will be released in October and continue through the fall and winter months. Listeners can hear candid conversations with community members about the parts of PEI’s heritage that often go unmentioned in history books.  

“It's been an incredible privilege to bring these fascinating stories and conversations to life through the hidden island podcast, said Season 6 producer Rafe Wright. “Every episode has given us the opportunity to explore another piece of the Island's rich history, and we've been fortunate to share that journey with some truly wonderful guests this year. Whether you're a history buff, or someone who simply enjoys a great story, this season has something for you." 

Season six features remarkable guests and thought-provoking conversations, each offering a unique perspective on PEI’s heritage. 

Episodes include:

  • Lost for Words: PEI’s Forgotten Gaelic History
  • Guided by Light: A Journey of PEI Lighthouse Stories
  • Ladies of the Land: The Women Protecting PEI’s Natural History
  • Ghosts on the Gulf: Exploring PEI’s Most Spine-tingling Tales

Additional episodes explore a variety of other Island stories and perspectives. 

Listeners can find more information and listen to past episodes at https://www.peimuseum.ca/thehiddenisland or find it wherever they get their podcasts.

"One of the strengths of this project is the way it connects Islanders with their shared heritage through the stories of people, places and events that have helped shape our province. There are countless stories still waiting to be told, and I encourage Islanders to bring forward ideas that could inspire future episodes of hidden island."

-Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson

Those with ideas for future episodes or video features are encouraged to contact the project coordinator at thehiddenisland@gov.pe.ca.

For more information or to listen to the season six trailer visit https://www.peimuseum.ca/thehiddenisland

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
Email: charlotte_digness@gov.nt.ca
